chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Ali ibn Abi Rashid, from Ibrahim ibn al-Sindi, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I described to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) the ones who speak with this matter (Wilayah) from those who perform the work of the Sultan (ruling authority), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'When they rule over you, they will bring leniency upon you and benefit you in your needs.' I said: 'Among them are those who do that and among them are those who do not.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one among them who does not do that, disavow him, as Allah (exalted be He) disavows him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a righteous ruler according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In the context of the Minor and Major Occultations, this hadith provides a pragmatic criterion for political legitimacy, shifting focus from mere title to functional justice. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines righteous rule by the alleviation of burdens and fulfillment of needs, establishing a basis for 'bara'ah' (disavowal) against those who fail in this duty, a concept central to Shia political theology regarding the evaluation of contemporary authorities.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from Ali Bin Abu Rashid, from Ibrahim Bin Al Sandy, from Yunus Bin Ammar who said,

‘I described to Abu Abdullahasws the ones who are speaking with this matter (Wilayah) from the ones who are office-bearers of the Sultan (ruling authority), so heasws said: ‘When they rule over you they would be including the leniency over you and they would be benefitting you regarding your needs’. I said, ‘Among them are the ones who do that and among them are ones who don’t’. Heasws said: ‘The one who does not do that so disavow from him by the Disavowing of Allahazwj from him’.
en.sarwar: 14. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqiy from Ali ibn abu Rashid from Ibrahim ibn al-Sindiy from Yunus ibn Hammad who has said the following: “

I once spoke to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about certain people who believe in Divine Authority of ‘A’immah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, but work for the Sultan. He (the Imam) said, ‘They have achieved authority, therefore, they benefit you and help you.’ I (the narrator) then said, ‘Certain ones among them do so and certain others do not do so. ‘He (the Imam) said, ‘You must denounce those of them who do not help and benefit you as Allah has denounced them.’”
